***Updated 2026-09-06***

**AES+F** is a Russian artist collective founded in Moscow and working internationally in contemporary art, photography, video, digital media and installation. The collective consists of **Tatiana Arzamasova, Lev Evzovich, Evgeny Svyatsky and Vladimir Fridkes**. AES+F is known particularly for large-scale, digitally constructed video installations and photographic works that examine contemporary social values, conflict, desire and mass culture. [1][2]

{{page:image}}

{{page:credit}}

## History

AES+F was formed in **1987** as the AES Group by Tatiana Arzamasova, Lev Evzovich and Evgeny Svyatsky. In **1995**, photographer Vladimir Fridkes joined the group, after which it adopted the name AES+F. The four members brought different professional backgrounds to the collective: Arzamasova and Evzovich were trained as architects, Svyatsky worked in graphic and book design, and Fridkes had a career in fashion photography. [1]

The collective's early practice incorporated conceptual architecture, photography, graphic design, painting, sculpture and installation. Its later work increasingly combined photography and computer-generated imagery with video and large-scale digital installations. AES+F describes its practice as a form of "social psychoanalysis" concerned with contemporary global culture and its values, vices and conflicts. [1]

## Members

### Tatiana Arzamasova

Tatiana Arzamasova was born in 1955 and graduated from the Moscow Architectural Institute in 1978. Before the formation of AES, she worked in conceptual architecture and participated in exhibitions of conceptual architecture in London, Paris and Venice. [1]

### Lev Evzovich

Lev Evzovich was born in 1958 and graduated from the Moscow Architectural Institute in 1982. His professional background includes conceptual architecture, animation and film art direction. [1]

### Evgeny Svyatsky

Evgeny Svyatsky was born in 1957 and graduated from the Moscow University of Printing Arts in 1980. He worked in book illustration, advertising, graphic and poster design and served as a creative director for publishing houses in Moscow. [1]

### Vladimir Fridkes

Vladimir Fridkes was born in Moscow in 1956 and worked as a fashion photographer before joining AES. His photographs were published in international fashion magazines including *Vogue*, *Harper's Bazaar*, *ELLE*, *Marie Claire* and *Cosmopolitan*. His background in fashion photography became one of the distinctive elements of the collective's later visual language. [1]

## The Liminal Space Trilogy

AES+F achieved international recognition with **The Liminal Space Trilogy**, a series of large-scale multimedia works consisting of *Last Riot*, *The Feast of Trimalchio* and *Allegoria Sacra*. The trilogy uses contemporary environments and digitally manipulated imagery to reinterpret historical ideas of violence, pleasure, morality, paradise and purgatory. [1][3]

### Last Riot

**Last Riot** was produced between 2005 and 2008 and is the first part of the trilogy. It consists of multichannel video installations, video stills, digital collages, drawings and sculptures. The work presents an artificial world of perpetual conflict populated by young, androgynous figures whose violence resembles the logic of a video game. [3]

*Last Riot* was presented in the Russian Pavilion at the **52nd Venice Biennale in 2007**, bringing AES+F significant international attention. [1][4]

### The Feast of Trimalchio

**The Feast of Trimalchio**, completed in 2009, is the second part of the trilogy. It takes its title from the extravagant banquet described in Petronius's *Satyricon* and transfers the idea of excess into a contemporary visual environment. The work was presented in Venice in 2009. [1][2]

### Allegoria Sacra

**Allegoria Sacra**, begun in 2011, is the third and final part of the trilogy. The work takes inspiration from Giovanni Bellini's painting *Allegoria Sacra* and relocates the idea of purgatory to a futuristic international airport. The installation combines video, photography, digital collage and painting. [1][5]

The project was first presented at the **4th Moscow Biennale of Contemporary Art** in 2011. The complete trilogy was subsequently presented at venues including the Martin-Gropius-Bau in Berlin and the Central Exhibition Hall Manege in Moscow. [1][5]

## Inverso Mundus

**Inverso Mundus**, created in 2015, was presented at the **56th Venice Biennale**. The project draws on the historical tradition of the *mundus inversus*, or inverted world, in which established social relationships are reversed. AES+F transforms this motif into a contemporary multimedia environment involving altered social roles, carnival imagery and digitally constructed scenes. [1][6]

The project continued the collective's interest in combining references from art history with contemporary popular imagery and digital technologies.

## Other projects

AES+F has produced projects extending beyond the Liminal Space Trilogy, including **Islamic Project**, **First Rider & Angels-Demons**, **Mare Mediterraneum**, **Psychosis**, **Turandot 2070** and **Digital Safari: Fables of the Jungle**. [1]

The collective has also worked in theatre and opera. Between 2016 and 2019, its members developed video and stage designs, including the video set design for *Psychosis*, based on Sarah Kane's *4.48 Psychosis*. In 2019, AES+F premiered *Turandot 2070*, a contemporary reinterpretation of Puccini's opera produced as an international theatrical collaboration. [1]

## Exhibitions and collections

AES+F has exhibited extensively at museums, biennials, festivals and galleries internationally. Its work has been shown at institutions including **Centre Pompidou** in Paris, **Tate Britain** in London, **Moderna Museet** in Stockholm, **ZKM** in Karlsruhe, **Mori Art Museum** in Tokyo, **Leeum Samsung Museum of Art** in Seoul and the **National Gallery of Australia** in Canberra. [1]

Works by the collective are held in international collections including Moderna Museet, MOCAK in Kraków, Sammlung Goetz in Munich, ZKM, the National Gallery of Australia, the Art Gallery of South Australia, Centre Pompidou and the Louis Vuitton Foundation. Its works are also represented in major Russian museum collections, including the State Tretyakov Gallery, the State Russian Museum and the Multimedia Art Museum in Moscow. [1]

## Awards

AES+F has received a number of international and Russian contemporary-art awards. The collective received the **Sergey Kuryokhin Contemporary Art Award** in 2011, the **main award of the Kandinsky Prize** in 2012, the **main award of NordArt Festival** in 2014 and the **Pino Pascali Prize** in 2015. These awards were associated with *Allegoria Sacra*. [1][7][8]

In 2015, the Fondazione Museo Pino Pascali awarded AES+F the 18th Pino Pascali Prize. The accompanying exhibition presented works from the collective's practice, including *Allegoria Sacra*. [8]

**Duncan Welgemoed** is a South African-born chef and cookbook author based in Adelaide, South Australia. He is the founder and co-owner of Africola, a restaurant opened in 2014 whose food and visual identity connect African culinary traditions with Adelaide's hospitality and design culture. In 2026, he also appeared in ADL Fashion Week's campaign *The Threads Between Us*. **[1][2][3]**

{{page:image}}

{{page:credit}}

## Background and career

Welgemoed grew up in Johannesburg and subsequently near the Mozambique border before working in kitchens in Britain. He was head chef at The Goose at Britwell Salome when the restaurant received a Michelin star in 2005, and also worked at Le Manoir aux Quat'Saisons. He moved to South Australia in 2010. **[1][4]**

In Adelaide, he worked at Bistro Dom before opening Africola with designer James Brown in 2014. Brown, a co-owner and director of Mash Design, contributed to the restaurant's graphic identity and interiors. **[2][4]**

## Africola and culinary approach

Africola initially drew on South African cooking, including braai and Cape Malay influences. In 2016, the restaurant changed its menu and interior, shifting towards North African and Maghreb references. In a 2017 interview, Welgemoed described a greater emphasis on vegetables, grains and a broader range of spices, while retaining smoke and fire as essential cooking tools. **[2]**

The collaboration with Brown made visual presentation part of the restaurant's identity as well as its food. SBS documented the connection between its bold graphics, redesigned dining room and changing culinary direction. Welgemoed has also described Africola as an informal social environment supported by relationships with local producers and its regular customers. **[2][4]**

## Books

Welgemoed's *Africola: Slow Food, Fast Words, Cult Chef* appeared in 2020. Its recipes extend the restaurant's approach to home cooking, including vegetable dishes, fermentation, condiments and pickles. **[1][5]**

*Cooking with Fire: Aussie BBQ with a South African Twist* was published by Affirm Press on 24 September 2024. The 224-page book brings together Australian and South African barbecue references, covering meat, vegetables and outdoor cooking. **[6]**

## Fashion and Adelaide's creative community

Welgemoed was one of the subjects of *The Threads Between Us*, the 2026 ADL Fashion Week campaign. Other participants included [Vanessa Pearce](/vanessa-pearce) of The Wolf Gang, Rachel Van Brussel, broadcaster Bel Sloane, and George and Pat Georgiou of Alexis George. The campaign presented hospitality, fashion and personal style as connected parts of Adelaide's creative life. **[3]**

Maxim Koshkarev is a Russian naval officer who became the principal defendant in a 2026 criminal investigation concerning alleged forgeries of works attributed to Soviet-American sculptor Ernst Neizvestny. At the time of the investigation, Koshkarev held the rank of captain second rank and was deputy chief of staff of the Russian Navy's Northern Fleet. Investigators allege that between 2020 and 2026 he organized the production and sale of at least 30 works presented as works by Neizvestny. [1][2]

## Military career

Publicly available reporting identifies Koshkarev as a career Russian naval officer and former deputy chief of staff of the Northern Fleet. Detailed biographical information about his education, earlier appointments and personal life has not been widely published by authoritative sources.

According to reporting based on investigative materials, the investigation initially concerned Koshkarev in connection with other activities and subsequently identified his alleged involvement in the production and circulation of counterfeit artworks. Media reports have also described his interest in numismatics and military antiques, including purchases and sales discussed on specialist internet forums. These reports do not by themselves establish a connection between those activities and the alleged forgery scheme. [3]

## Ernst Neizvestny case

On 29 May 2026, the Russian Investigative Committee announced criminal proceedings against Koshkarev over the alleged production and sale of counterfeit paintings and sculptures attributed to Ernst Neizvestny. He was charged under Article 146 of the Russian Criminal Code concerning unlawful use of copyrighted works and Article 159 concerning fraud on an especially large scale. Investigators alleged that the works were produced without the consent of the copyright holders and subsequently sold to private collectors in Russia and abroad. [1][4]

Investigators stated that at least 30 works had been produced between 2020 and 2026 and that the alleged group had received more than 90 million rubles from their sale. Searches conducted during the investigation resulted in the seizure of 37 paintings and 10 sculptures, which were sent for expert examination. [1][4]

Koshkarev was detained on 28 April 2026 and placed under house arrest. According to *Kommersant*, he acknowledged his guilt. His property valued at more than 128 million rubles was subsequently reported to have been placed under arrest as part of measures intended to secure compensation for alleged damage. [2]

### Connection with the Tretyakov Gallery exhibition

The investigation became publicly known in connection with the exhibition **The Epoch of Neizvestny. For the Artist's Centenary**, held at the New Tretyakov Gallery from 16 December 2025 to 12 May 2026. Investigators searched the gallery and examined works associated with the case. [4][5]

The exact relationship between the alleged forgeries and the exhibition has been disputed in media reports. *Kommersant* reported that counterfeit works were discovered in connection with the exhibition, while *The Art Newspaper Russia* subsequently noted that it was premature to conclude that identified counterfeit works had actually been displayed. The exhibition included works from both museum and private collections, and the authenticity of seized objects was still being examined. [5][6]

The case later expanded beyond Koshkarev. In September 2026, investigators accused art-market professionals Liubov Agafonova and Roza Verkhovina of involvement in the alleged scheme. Both had previously been identified as injured parties in the investigation and were placed under house arrest on 9 September 2026. [6][7]

## Chronology

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 2020–2026 | Investigators allege that Koshkarev and other members of a group organized the production and sale of at least 30 works attributed to Ernst Neizvestny. [1] |
| 28 April 2026 | Koshkarev was detained and placed under house arrest. [2] |
| 29 May 2026 | The Investigative Committee publicly announced the criminal case and identified Koshkarev as a defendant. [1][4] |
| 29 May 2026 | Investigators reported searches and the seizure of paintings and sculptures for examination. [4] |
| June 2026 | Russian and international media reported conflicting information about whether suspected forgeries had been displayed at the New Tretyakov Gallery. [5][6] |
| 9 September 2026 | Liubov Agafonova and Roza Verkhovina were placed under house arrest after being charged in connection with the case. [7] |

## Legal status

As of September 2026, the case remains under investigation. The allegations concerning the production, attribution and sale of counterfeit works are subject to criminal proceedings and expert examination. The charges and investigative allegations should not be treated as a final judicial determination of guilt.

Анна Харви (12 сентября 1944 – 9 октября 2018) была выдающейся фигурой в мире моды и журналистики[2]. Ее карьера в Condé Nast Publications продолжалась более 30 лет, где она занимала ряд ключевых позиций:

## Карьера в модной индустрии

- Начала работу в Harper's & Queen (ныне Harper's Bazaar) вместе с Анной Винтур
- Присоединилась к Condé Nast в 1970 году как директор моды журнала Brides
- Работала заместителем редактора Tatler и директором моды British Vogue
- В 1997 году стала редакционным директором Condé Nast New Markets[2]

## Работа с принцессой Дианой

Анна Харви сыграла ключевую роль в формировании стиля принцессы Дианы:

- Познакомилась с Дианой в 1980 году, когда та была еще леди Дианой Спенсер[2]
- Помогла трансформировать стиль Дианы от простых нарядов Laura Ashley до статуса иконы стиля[3]
- Познакомила принцессу с такими брендами, как Moschino, Versace и Emilio Pucci[3]
- Сотрудничала с дизайнерами Кэтрин Уокер, Жаком Азагури и Versace для создания образов Дианы[2]

## Влияние на модную индустрию

- Способствовала продвижению многих известных фотографов, дизайнеров и модных фигур, включая Стивена Мейзела, Брюса Вебера и Изабеллу Блоу[2]
- Работала с такими моделями, как Кейт Мосс, Наоми Кэмпбелл и Линда Евангелиста[2]
- В 1986 году Harpers & Queen назвал Харви 23-й самой влиятельной персоной в Британии[2]

## Личный стиль и советы

Анна Харви была известна своим безупречным вкусом и давала ценные советы по стилю:

- Считала, что одежду не стоит делить на возрастные группы[1]
- Рекомендовала обновлять гардероб, так как крой и стиль одежды меняются со временем[1]
- Советовала покупать две одинаковые вещи, если они идеально подходят[1]
- Выступала за комфорт в одежде, но против полностью спортивных образов[1]

Анна Харви оставила значительный след в мире моды, влияя на стиль как членов королевской семьи, так и обычных людей через свою работу в журналах и книгу "Стиль вне времени"[1][3].
